title: Separating levels of bounded arithmetic
formal:
Are there integers \(i>j\ge1\) and a closed first-order arithmetic sentence \(\theta\) such that
\[T_2^i\vdash\theta\qquad\text{and}\qquad T_2^j\nvdash\theta?\]
The theory \(T_2^r\) is BASIC together with induction for every \(\Sigma_r^b\) formula in the language defined below. The question asks for a separation as sets of provable sentences, with no assumed separation of computational complexity classes and no additional oracle symbols. One pair of levels is enough; it need not be fixed in advance, and proving strictness at every pair is not required.
why: These theories organize arithmetic reasoning by the logical complexity permitted in induction hypotheses. Showing that even two positive levels prove different sentences would establish an unconditional difference in the strength of those reasoning principles. It would clarify how computational complexity is reflected in provability, beyond the known conditional connections.
status_note: Individual source and formulation review on 2026-09-14. Oliveira’s 2025 Open Problem 5.5 and the book’s complete theory definition were checked. Ježil–Tsintsilidas, arXiv:2602.19934v1 (February 2026), explicitly retain removal of assumptions in their hierarchy separations as an open problem. A bounded subsequent search found no matching unconditional separation or proof that all positive levels coincide. This records the checked sources and search limits, not exhaustive certification of present openness.

sentences: The question asks whether two positive levels of Buss’s bounded-arithmetic hierarchy prove different sentences.
Each level has the same basic arithmetic axioms but permits induction for a different class of bounded formulas.
A solution may choose any two distinct positive levels and must prove an unconditional difference in their deductive strength.
The full axiom list, formula grammar and induction scheme specify the theories without relying on an unstated standard model.
Recent conditional separations do not provide the unconditional nonprovability witness required here.

definitions:
Use classical first-order logic with equality and the one-sorted language \(L=\{0,1,+,\cdot,H,\ell,\#,\le\}\). Here \(H\) and \(\ell\) are unary, \(+\), \(\cdot\), \(\#\) are binary, and \(\le\) is a binary predicate. Terms are the finite expressions formed from variables, these constants and these function symbols. Atomic formulas are equalities or inequalities between terms. The logical operations are negation, conjunction, disjunction and first-order universal/existential quantification; implication and equivalence abbreviate their usual Boolean expansions. The successor notation \(Sx\) abbreviates \(x+1\), \(2\) abbreviates \(1+1\), and \(2x\) means \(2\cdot x\).

The intended standard structure has domain \(\mathbb N=\{0,1,\ldots\}\), its usual addition, multiplication and order, \(H(x)=\lfloor x/2\rfloor\), \(\ell(0)=0\), \(\ell(x)=\lfloor\log_2 x\rfloor+1\) for \(x>0\), and \(x\#y=2^{\ell(x)\ell(y)}\). This interpretation explains the symbols; the theory's nonlogical axioms are exactly the following finite BASIC list and the specified induction scheme, rather than all sentences true in this standard structure. Every free variable in the following displays is universally quantified.

The order and successor axioms are
\[\begin{gathered}
a\le b\ \to\ a\le b+1,\qquad a\ne a+1,\qquad 0\le a,\\
(a\le b\land a\ne b)\ \to\ a+1\le b,\qquad a\ne0\ \to\ 2a\ne0,\\
a\le b\lor b\le a,\qquad (a\le b\land b\le a)\ \to\ a=b,\\
(a\le b\land b\le c)\ \to\ a\le c,\qquad a\le a+b,\\
(a\le b\land a\ne b)\ \to\ (2a+1\le2b\land 2a+1\ne2b).
\end{gathered}\]
The addition and multiplication axioms are
\[\begin{gathered}
a+b=b+a,\qquad a+0=a,\qquad a+(b+1)=(a+b)+1,\\
(a+b)+c=a+(b+c),\qquad a+b\le a+c\ \to\ b\le c,\\
a\cdot0=0,\qquad a\cdot(b+1)=a\cdot b+a,\qquad a\cdot b=b\cdot a,\\
a\cdot(b+c)=(a\cdot b)+(a\cdot c),\\
1\le a\ \to\ ((a\cdot b\le a\cdot c)\leftrightarrow(b\le c)).
\end{gathered}\]
The length, halving and smash axioms are
\[\begin{gathered}
\ell(0)=0,\qquad \ell(1)=1,\qquad a\le b\ \to\ \ell(a)\le\ell(b),\\
a\ne0\ \to\ (\ell(2a)=\ell(a)+1\land\ell(2a+1)=\ell(a)+1),\\
\ell(a\#b)=\ell(a)\cdot\ell(b)+1,\qquad 0\#a=1,\\
a\ne0\ \to\ (1\#(2a)=2(1\#a)\land1\#(2a+1)=2(1\#a)),\\
a\#b=b\#a,\qquad \ell(a)=\ell(b)\ \to\ a\#c=b\#c,\\
\ell(a)=\ell(b)+\ell(c)\ \to\ a\#d=(b\#d)\cdot(c\#d),\\
a\ne0\ \to\ \ell(a)=\ell(H(a))+1,\\
a=H(b)\ \leftrightarrow\ (2a=b\lor2a+1=b).
\end{gathered}\]
These are the 32 axioms in Krajíček's Definition 5.2.1, regrouped by operation, with \(H\) and \(\ell\) replacing the printed halving and length notation. No sequence function or oracle predicate is added.

For a term \(t\) not containing \(y\), write \(\exists y\le t\,\psi\) for \(\exists y(y\le t\land\psi)\), and \(\forall y\le t\,\psi\) for \(\forall y(y\le t\to\psi)\). These are bounded quantifiers. They are sharply bounded when the bound is explicitly \(\ell(t)\). The bound may contain other free variables. Let \(\Sigma_0^b=\Pi_0^b\) be all formulas built from atomic formulas using Boolean operations and only sharply bounded quantifiers. Recursively, \(\Sigma_{r+1}^b,\Pi_{r+1}^b\) are the smallest pair of classes satisfying: both contain \(\Sigma_r^b\cup\Pi_r^b\); both are closed under conjunction, disjunction and both sharply bounded quantifiers; \(\Sigma_{r+1}^b\) is closed under bounded existential quantification; \(\Pi_{r+1}^b\) is closed under bounded universal quantification; and negation sends either class into the other. These are the full formula classes, allowing sharply bounded quantifiers inside as well as outside the other quantifiers, rather than only a strict prenex fragment.

For a set \(T\) of closed axioms, \(T\vdash\theta\) means that the closed sentence \(\theta\) has a finite proof in classical first-order logic with equality from those axioms. Equivalently, every nonempty \(L\)-structure satisfying all axioms of \(T\) satisfies \(\theta\). This equivalence is first-order completeness; structures in this characterization are not restricted to the standard natural numbers. There is no bound on proof length. Equality of theories here means equality of their deductive closures in the same language.

For each integer \(r\ge1\), \(T_2^r\) has the displayed BASIC axioms and, for each \(\varphi(x,\vec a)\in\Sigma_r^b\), the universal closure over all parameter variables \(\vec a\) of
\[\bigl(\varphi(0,\vec a)\land\forall x(\varphi(x,\vec a)\to\varphi(x+1,\vec a))\bigr)\ \to\ \forall x\,\varphi(x,\vec a).\]
Parameters are allowed and are not required to be numerals. There are no induction axioms for formulas outside the specified class unless they are consequences of these axioms. Since the formula classes are nested, \(T_2^j\subseteq T_2^i\) in deductive strength when \(j<i\). A positive answer therefore gives a strict inclusion. The separating sentence may have unrestricted first-order quantifiers; no complexity or syntactic bound on that witness sentence is part of the target.

The indices, finite formulas and finite proofs in the question range over ordinary standard mathematical objects. The nonprovability claim is external: it means that no finite proof from the weaker theory exists, rather than asking the weaker theory itself to prove its inability. A countermodel for the weaker theory and the sentence is an equivalent way to certify that nonprovability. A positive answer must be unconditional in the usual mathematical metatheory; adding an unproved complexity assumption changes the requested statement.
answer_criterion: Supply a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked proof or refutation of the displayed existential separation. A positive answer must establish one pair of standard integers \(i>j\ge1\), a closed sentence provable in \(T_2^i\), and its nonprovability in \(T_2^j\); the latter can equivalently be proved by a model of \(T_2^j\) falsifying the sentence. A negative answer must establish equality of the deductive closures for every pair \(i>j\ge1\). A difference between axiom lists, a lower bound on the shortest proof of a still-provable sentence, a relativized separation, or a separation conditional on an unproved complexity conjecture does not settle this target.

context_blocks.text: Open Problem 5.5 asks to separate some two levels with positive indices. This is not a request to select one predetermined pair or to give proof-length lower bounds. The survey places it alongside the question of whether feasible arithmetic can prove that P equals NP.

The complete finite axiom list matters because the target concerns formal provability, not only the intended meaning of addition and binary length. The model above uses the book’s first-order language without its optional sequence-function extension.

The 2026 preprint extends conditional comparisons between theories with different induction and bounded collection principles. Its introduction recalls the implication from noncollapse of the polynomial hierarchy to noncollapse of bounded arithmetic, and Section 1.3 expressly leaves unconditional separations open. This is progress on related conditional statements, not a claimed unconditional witness for this card.
